full_name: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
mission: An interdisciplinary initiative at Stanford HAI that 'makes fundamental advances in the study, development, and deployment of foundation models'. Its safety-relevant work is evaluation and transparency: the HELM benchmark, the Foundation Model Transparency Index and AI policy support for governments. Director: Percy Liang.

key_work.title: On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models
key_work.plain_summary: The 200-page report that coined 'foundation models' and laid out their capabilities, risks and societal impacts.

key_work.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
key_work.plain_summary: A broad, transparent benchmark that scores language models on accuracy plus robustness, fairness, toxicity and more, across many scenarios.

key_work.title: Foundation Model Transparency Index
key_work.plain_summary: Scores major AI developers on how much they disclose about data, compute, risks and usage; found widespread opacity.

people.role: Director; associate professor of computer science

warnings.text: Foundation models 'present novel capabilities and risks that are poorly understood. Nonetheless, they are being deployed at scale' (homepage).
Major developers disclose too little about training data, risks and downstream use (Transparency Index).

recommendations.text: Evaluate models holistically and transparently across many risks, not just accuracy (HELM).
Increase developer transparency and support evidence-based AI policy across jurisdictions.
